data.title: Minocycline (oral + topical foam)
data.summary: II Antibiotics — a) Tetracyclines · Second-generation semisynthetic tetracycline — the most lipophilic
data.body:
_Oral · II Antibiotics — a) Tetracyclines_

**Class:** Second-generation semisynthetic tetracycline — the most lipophilic

## Mechanism of action
- Binds the 30S ribosome and blocks protein synthesis (bacteriostatic)
- Anti-inflammatory: inhibits MMPs, neutrophil chemotaxis and lymphocyte activity
- High lipophilicity → good penetration into the pilosebaceous unit, CNS and skin

## Pharmacokinetics
- Almost completely absorbed; food has little effect; still chelated by metal ions
- Half-life 11–22 h; metabolised mainly in the liver

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne vulgaris (second choice after doxycycline because of its safety profile)
- Leprosy: part of the ROM regimen (rifampicin, ofloxacin, minocycline) and an alternative drug
- Atypical mycobacteria (especially M. marinum), Nocardia, community MRSA
- Rosacea; anti-inflammatory use in bullous pemphigoid, sarcoidosis, CARP

## Dose & formulations
- Acne: 50–100 mg twice daily, or extended-release 1 mg/kg once daily
- Leprosy: 100 mg daily (alternative regimens); ROM monthly: 100 mg as part of the single monthly dose

## Adverse effects
- Vestibular toxicity (dizziness, vertigo, ataxia) — commoner in women
- Hyperpigmentation — Type I: blue-black in scars and inflamed sites (iron/haemosiderin stains); Type II: blue-grey on normal skin of shins and forearms (iron and melanin); Type III: muddy-brown diffuse in sun-exposed skin (melanin)
- Pigmentation can also affect teeth (even adult teeth), nails, sclera, oral mucosa, thyroid ('black thyroid') and bone
- Autoimmune: drug-induced lupus (often p-ANCA positive), autoimmune hepatitis, serum-sickness-like reaction, polyarteritis-like vasculitis
- Hypersensitivity syndrome (DRESS) in the first weeks, pneumonitis
- Less phototoxic than doxycycline; pseudotumor cerebri

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy, breastfeeding, children under 8 years
- Lupus or autoimmune hepatitis history; concurrent oral retinoids

## Drug interactions
- Metal ions and antacids reduce absorption
- Isotretinoin/acitretin: pseudotumor cerebri
- Warfarin effect may increase

## Monitoring
- No routine tests for short courses
- For courses beyond a few months: watch for pigmentation, joint pain, rash, and check LFT/ANA if symptoms

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (old FDA category D). Avoid in breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Most lipophilic tetracycline → vestibular side effects and best CNS penetration
- Three types of pigmentation — be able to describe them
- Autoimmune side effects: drug-induced lupus and autoimmune hepatitis
- Least phototoxic of the commonly used tetracyclines
- Used in leprosy (ROM)

## Topical form: Minocycline 4% topical foam
_Tetracycline antibiotic in a hydrophobic foam base (topical minocycline foam)_

**Mechanism**
- Binds the 30S ribosome; anti-inflammatory (MMP inhibition, neutrophil effects)
- Topical delivery gives high follicular levels with negligible blood levels — avoids systemic minocycline side effects

**Indications**
- Moderate–severe inflammatory acne (4% foam, age 9 and over)
- Papulopustular rosacea (1.5% foam)

**Dose & how to apply**
- Apply once daily at about the same time, at least 1 h before bathing/sleep; avoid fire (flammable)

**Adverse effects**
- Mild irritation; possible hyperpigmentation (rare)
- Theoretically tooth discolouration in children under 8 — not used in that age group

**Contraindications**
- Hypersensitivity to tetracyclines; children under 9

**Pregnancy:** Avoid in pregnancy (tetracycline class).

**Viva points**
- Topical tetracycline that avoids vestibular and autoimmune side effects of oral minocycline
- Foam is flammable

_Note: The exam list says 4% gel; the approved product is minocycline 4% foam (acne) and 1.5% foam (rosacea), so it is listed as a foam. Topical minocycline is not described in Wolverton 4e or Khopkar; added at your request._

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.9; Khopkar ch.1; Not covered in Wolverton 4e or Khopkar (newer product); product information (Amzeeq/Zilxi). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
